newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-TIMELINES - Today in History - March 11.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-TIMELINES - Today in History - March 11.

text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Pioneer pastoralist "Squire" SAMUEL PHILLIPS, who ran an English style property at Culham in Western Australia, was born on this day in 1819.
British sugar magnate SIR HENRY TATE was born in 1819.
British holder of the world speed records on land and sea, SIR MALCOLM CAMPBELL, was born in 1885.

Australian radio pioneer GEORGE EDWARDS, known as "the man with a thousand voices", was born in 1886. His shows such as "Darby and Joan", "Dad and Dave" and "Scott of Scotland Yard" were so popular that when his wife NELL STIRLING had their child in 1942, fans - mailed in 30,000 hand-knitted baby outfits.
RAOUL WALSH, U.S. film director, was born in 1892. In films from 1914, he was best known for his American gangster films "High Sierra", "White Heat" and "The Roaring Twenties".
British Labour Prime Minister (1964-67, 1974-76) HAROLD WILSON, was born in 1916.
Australian author NANCY CATO, whose best-known work is "All The Rivers Run", was born in 1917.
Australian historian GEOFFREY BLAINEY was born in 1930.
Zany British author DOUGLAS ADAMS, known for "The Hitch-Hiker's Guide to the Galaxy" which began as a radio serial and then became a book and a television series, was born in 1952.
Australian media tycoon and chief of News Corporation, RUPERT KEITH MURDOCH, who became an American citizen in 1985, was born in 1931.
Australian squash legend GEOFF HUNT was born in 1947.
Dutch guitarist GEORGE KOOYMANS was born in 1948. He was a songwriter and leader of the 'Golden Earring'. Their hits included "Radar Love" (1973) and "Twilight Zone" (1982).
The man who had an international hit with "Don't Worry Be Happy" BOBBY McFERRIN was born in 1950. The song was from the film "Cocktail".
US singer and songwriter LENNY WOLF was born in 1962. He was with the heavy metal group 'Kingdom Come'.
** EVENTS **
1702 : England's first daily paper, the DAILY COURANT,
was published.
1845 : In New Zealand, further Maori uprisings occurred
against British rule.
1864 : 250 people died when a dam in the North of England
burst its banks and flooded the surrounding region.
1930 : "The Intimate Revue" suffered every first night

theatrical problem imaginable, and didn't make a second night. At first the curtains at the theatre refused to open, when they did, actors were revealed whose costumes didn't fit, the actors then had difficulty remembering their lines, and finally it took 25 minutes to change scenery between each brief sketch. No wonder it didn't run for more than one night !
1941 : The American Congress passed the Lend Lease Act,
which allowed Allied countries to receive tanks and ships etc. on credit from the United States, to continue their campaigns in World War Two.
1955 : SIR ALEXANDER FLEMING, the Scottish bacteriologist
who discovered penicillin, died.
1957 : The American lawyer and author ERLE STANLEY
GARDNER, who created "PERRY MASON", died.
1985 : MIKHAIL SERGEYEVICH GORBACHEV took over the
leadership of the Soviet Community Party following the death of KONSTANTIN CHERNENKO.
1985 : Britain's popular Harrods store was bought by the
wealthy cotton-brokers from Cairo, the FAYED brothers.
1988 : South African golf champion ARTHUR D'ARCY LOCKE
died.
1988 : Britain dropped the pound-note, replacing it with
a pound-coin.
1990 : American tennis star JENNIFER CAPRIATI played her
first professional match at the age of 13.
1994 : The IRA was blamed for a series of mortar attacks
on London's Heathrow Airport.
